title: The universal closed-immersion locus in the base is open
statement: Let $B,A,C$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $p:A\to B$ and $q:C\to B$ be morphisms, and let $f:A\to C$ satisfy $q\circ f=p$. Assume $p$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism], and assume $q$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. There is an open subscheme $V\subseteq B$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that for every scheme $T$ and morphism $h:T\to B$, the base change $f_T:A\times_BT\to C\times_BT$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] if and only if $h$ factors through $V\hookrightarrow B$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-closed-graph-universally-closed-diagram] to the given commutative triangle: $p$ is universally closed and $q$ is separated by hypothesis. It gives universal closedness of every $f_T$ and of $p_2=p\circ\operatorname{pr}_1:A\times_C A\to B$, and gives closedness of the underlying maps of $p$ and $p_2$.

source.place: Tag 05XA, spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-where-closed-immersion, universally closedness and relative self-product paragraph; expanded via Tag 04NX.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-universal-unramified-radicial-open]. Its local finite type hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis on $p$, and its closedness hypotheses on $p$ and $A\times_C A\to B$ are step 1. Obtain an open $V\subseteq B$ such that, for every scheme $T$ and every $h:T\to B$, $h$ factors through $V$ if and only if $f_T$ is unramified and universally injective.

Fix any scheme $T$ and $h:T\to B$. The morphism $g=f_T$ is universally closed by step 1, so [lem-sfb-universally-closed-unramified-radicial-criterion] identifies its being unramified and universally injective with its being a closed immersion. Combining this equivalence with step 2 gives $f_T$ a closed immersion if and only if $h$ factors through $V$. This holds for all $T,h$, with the same $V$, as required.
